summary: bip32-js postinstall exfiltrates SSH keys, cloud credentials, and crypto wallet material to webhook.site
details: The package's postinstall.js runs automatically on npm install and harvests installer-owned secrets: it reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa, id_ed25519, and id_ecdsa; ~/.aws/credentials;.env files;.npmrc; the Solana keypair at ~/.config/solana/id.json; and Ethereum keystore files. It also walks hidden home subdirectories collecting files whose names match wallet, key, secret, seed, mnemonic, keystore, or private (with.json/.pem extensions). The collected file contents are bundled together with os.hostname() and os.userInfo().username and POSTed over HTTPS to https://webhook.site/5c5ad6cb-62df-4ea5-9dfb-2c447920ddc4, a hardcoded attacker-controlled endpoint. The package name mimics the legitimate bip32 library to lure cryptocurrency developers whose machines contain wallet material.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
